tr.td: A statement of how to put guidance into practice, printed in a publication whose publicationType is implementation-guidance or methodology: the handbook's "products that are not guidelines" (§1.9), a "how to" document that makes no recommendations of its own. Not a recommendation, and not a good practice statement — both are made by a guideline and approved by the GRC; this is neither. It carries no kind, direction, strength or certainty, because nothing graded it. A handbook's own "Best practices" lists are the typical source. Owner ruling 1b, 2026-10-12: model these as their own class, not as recommendation nodes of a new kind.

A node in the ingested library L1 is read from: a source document, a section or a block, addressed by the library's own IRI. Opaque, as L1 asserts nothing about the library's internal model; the library is upstream, so pointing at it keeps the layering rule.
